definition: A lightweight foam-lined shell with vents and a chin strap, worn on the head by bicycle riders to cushion falls.
A hard, full-coverage shell with a padded lining, visor and chin strap, worn on the head by motorbike riders to absorb impact.
A rigid, velvet-covered cap with a chin harness, worn on the head by horse riders to cushion the skull in a fall.
A body-worn vest containing layers of tough fibre or plates, made to stop bullets and fragments hitting the chest and back.
A fitted vest lined with dense woven layers and plates, worn under or over other layers to stop knife blades reaching the body.
A set of shaped, hinged steel plates strapped over the body, made to shield a mounted knight from blows in battle.
A rigid, brimmed helmet of moulded plastic with an inner cradle, worn on building sites to shield the head from falling objects.
Heavy leather boots with a reinforced toe cap and thick grippy sole, worn on building sites and factory floors to protect the feet.
A hood with a dark tinted window that darkens against the glare, held in front of the face while joining metal with an arc.
Glasses with darkened lenses that cut glare and block ultraviolet light, worn over the eyes in bright sun.
A buoyant vest, inflated or foam-filled, worn over the torso so a person in water floats with the face above the surface.
A moulded seat with a padded shell and harness straps, fixed to a vehicle seat to hold a small child securely while travelling.
A thin sheath of latex or similar material rolled over the penis before intercourse, to stop pregnancy and the spread of infections.
A lotion or spray rubbed onto exposed skin that absorbs or reflects ultraviolet rays, preventing burning during time in the sun.
A liquid, spray or lotion applied to skin and clothes whose smell and chemistry keep biting flies, midges and mosquitoes away.
A small ceiling-mounted unit that senses smoke particles in the air and sounds a loud siren to wake the people nearby.
A pressurised steel cylinder with a hose or nozzle and trigger, which sprays foam, powder or gas to put out a small blaze.
A boxed unit with a fan and filter that draws in room air and removes dust, pollen and smoke particles before blowing it out.
A fine mesh canopy hung over a bed or sleeping spot, which keeps biting insects away from the sleeper overnight.
A speaker cabinet with built-in electronics and volume and tone knobs that boosts the weak signal from an electric guitar to a loud sound.
A small metal box with a footswitch, plugged between an electric guitar and its amplifier to alter the sound with distortion, echo or similar changes.
A wide panel of sliding faders and knobs that blends many microphone and instrument signals into a balanced combined sound for recording or live speakers.
A flat-response loudspeaker used in recording rooms to reproduce music neutrally, so engineers can judge exactly what a recording sounds like.
A handheld or stand-mounted device with a sensitive capsule that turns spoken or sung sound into an electrical signal for amplifying or recording.
A small box with sockets and gain knobs that connects microphones and instruments to a computer, converting sound to digital data and back.
A flat console with two jog wheels, faders and pads, plugged into a computer to cue, blend and manipulate recorded music at a live event.
A keyboard with weighted keys and built-in speakers that plays recorded piano sounds electronically, usually with headphone output and a stand.
An electronic keyboard instrument that generates sound waves from circuits and lets the player shape pitch, tone and volume with dials and presets.
A compact electronic box with touch pads that plays programmed rhythm patterns from stored drum sounds for composing music.
A set of rubber or mesh pads on a frame, struck with sticks and wired to a module that plays recorded drum sounds through headphones.
A flat, thin touch-screen slab with a battery, used to browse the web, read, watch video and run downloaded programs without a keyboard.
A portable computer whose screen folds or detaches so it can be used either with its keyboard or held flat as a touch panel.
A pocket-sized touch-screen handset with a camera and mobile connection, used to call, message, browse and run downloadable programs.
Tiny cordless speakers that sit in the ear canal and receive sound over a radio link, with a charging case for storage.
A small folding knife whose blade swings into the handle, carried in a pocket for cutting string, fruit and similar everyday jobs.
A pair of pliers whose handles hide folding screwdrivers, a blade, a file and other small implements, carried on a belt or in a pocket.
A small hand-held device with a flint wheel or spark button and fuel reservoir that produces a flame to light tobacco or candles.
A slim, flat metal or leather box with a hinged lid that holds and protects a few cigarettes in a pocket or bag.
A lidded plastic or metal bottle carried around to hold drinking water, often with a screw cap or drinking nozzle.
A double-walled bottle with an airless gap between the walls and a screw lid, which keeps drinks hot or cold for hours.
A small lidded box of plastic or metal with a clasp, in which a packed midday meal is carried to school or work.
A hand-held writing instrument with an ink cartridge and ballpoint or nib, used to put words on paper.
A small bound pad of blank or ruled pages with a stiff cover, carried to jot down notes, lists and addresses.
A large frame-supported rucksack with padded shoulder straps and hip belt, made to carry clothes, food and shelter on long walks.
A flexible leakproof pouch with a drinking tube, carried inside a pack so a walker can sip water without stopping.
A cylinder with a bulb or LED, a reflector and a battery compartment that throws a beam of light when switched on.
A slender rod of wood or metal with a curved or knobbed handle, leaned on to steady each step when walking.
Thin strips of synthetic or mink hair stuck along the eyelid edge with glue to make the lashes look longer and fuller.
Pre-shaped plastic fingernail shells with an adhesive backing, pressed over the natural nails to give them a coloured or patterned finish.
Lengths of real or synthetic hair clipped, glued or sewn onto a person's own hair to add length or volume.
A cosmetic gel or powder of tiny sparkling flakes dabbed onto skin to make it shimmer at parties and festivals.
A printed transfer on thin film that is pressed onto skin with water, leaving an image that fades or washes off within days.
A cap of real or synthetic hair fitted over the head to change the wearer's look or cover a lack of natural hair.
A padded coat with thin wires or panels inside, wired to a rechargeable battery pack, that warms the wearer's torso in cold weather.
Insulated hand coverings with fine wires through the fingers and a small battery in the cuff, which keep hands warm in freezing air.
A dress-up outfit stitched with strings of small battery-powered lights that glow or flash in colours when switched on.
A glass or plastic-panelled building with a frame, kept warm by trapped sunlight, in which seedlings and tender plants are raised.
A long, arched frame of metal hoops covered with a sheet of heavy polythene, creating a warm sheltered space for growing vegetables.
A small wooden hut beside a plot of ground, where pots, compost and seed trays are stored and plants are started.
A small roofed hut with an opening in front, in which a dog sleeps or shelters outdoors.
A building divided into stalls with a roof and doors, in which horses are housed, fed and kept out of the weather.
A small raised wooden house with perches, nesting boxes and a wire run, in which hens sleep and lay eggs.
A raised wooden box with a mesh-fronted door and sleeping compartment, in which pet rabbits are kept.
A small wooden box with a round entry hole, fixed to a tree or post, in which small birds can nest.
A frame of metal or timber poles with seats hung from chains, anchored in the ground so children can swing back and forth.
A structure of linked bars, ladders and platforms that children scramble over, usually fixed in a yard.
A small wooden cabin built on platforms among the branches of a large tree, reached by a ladder, for children to play in.
A cooking cabinet with a door and heating elements, fitted into a gap in a row of base cabinets and wired directly to the supply.
A washing machine for crockery with a front panel matching the neighbouring cabinets, plumbed into the water supply and drain beneath the worktop.
A plumbed-in tank of resin beads fitted to the main water pipe that removes minerals from the supply to prevent scale.
A lamp holder wired into the ceiling, often with a shade or glass cover, which lights a whole room when switched on.
A wall-mounted box with shelves and a mirrored door, screwed to the wall above the basin to hold washing and shaving supplies.
A steel box with a combination or key lock, cemented into a wall or floor to protect papers and valuables from theft and fire.
Flat panels of silicon cells bolted to a roof that turn sunlight into electric current fed into the building's wiring.
A weatherproof unit fixed to a wall and wired to the mains, with a cable and plug that recharges an electric car's battery.
A line of timber panels or railings fixed to posts in the ground, marking and enclosing the boundary of a plot.
A tall slender pole, fixed upright in the ground or to a wall, with a rope and pulley for raising a flag.
A fixed week each year at a particular holiday apartment, bought outright so the owner may stay there during that week annually.
A marked rectangle of cemetery ground set aside, by purchase of an exclusive right, for the interment of one person's body.
A card or pass bought in advance that admits its holder to every home match or journey over a whole season.
A tamper-proof paper or fabric band fastened around the wrist that admits the wearer to a multi-day music event.
A movie bought from an online store and kept in the buyer's account for viewing whenever they like, with no disc.
A cosmetic appearance for a character or item in a video game, bought with money and unlocked in the player's online account.
A computer file holding the shapes of a complete alphabet in one typeface, installed so programs can display and print text in it.
A set of songs saved as ordinary compressed audio files on a drive, which can be copied and played on any device.
Digital image files made by scanning old prints, kept on a drive or online so the pictures can be viewed and copied.
An image file made on a drawing tablet and saved on a computer, containing a finished picture for viewing on screens.
A small glass, wooden or plastic ball or figure with a hook or loop, hung from the branches of a Christmas tree.
A fir-shaped frame of metal and plastic needles that slots together, set up indoors each December and packed away afterwards.
A life-sized hinged figure of white plastic bones, hung on a door or propped up to look spooky around October.
A small woven basket with a handle, lined with paper grass and filled with sweets and eggs for children to find.
A thin wax stick with a wick, pushed into a cake and lit, for the celebrated person to blow out.
A thin rubber or foil bag inflated with air or helium, tied with a string and hung or released at celebrations.
A small figurine or lettered piece placed on top of the uppermost tier of a marriage celebration cake.
A silky cord with a hanging fringed bundle and year charm, attached to a flat cap and moved across at the degree ceremony.
A hollow globe of red paper stretched over a bamboo frame with a candle or bulb inside, hung up at the lunar new year.
A metal cup or statuette on a plinth, presented to the winner of a contest and kept to commemorate the victory.
A heavy ornamented staff, usually of silver or gilt, carried before an official in procession as a symbol of authority.
A small wooden mallet struck on a block to call a courtroom or meeting to order.
A rectangle of cloth in a country's colours and pattern, flown from a pole to represent that nation.
A lidded vessel of metal, ceramic or wood designed to hold the ashes of a dead person.
A long box of wood or metal with a lid, in which a dead body is placed for funeral and burial.
A thin silvery disc holding a recorded movie in digital form, played on a disc player connected to a television.
A painting in oil on canvas of a named person, ordered from a painter who worked from sittings or photographs.
A small trinket bought at a place visited, such as a mug or magnet printed with its name, to remember the trip.
A flat engraved metal or stone sign mounted on a bench or wall, bearing the name and dates of a person who has died.
One small infant shoe, often bronzed or boxed, kept by parents as a memento of the child's earliest steps.
A stamped metal disc on a ribbon, awarded to a soldier for service in a particular war or operation.
A bound book of dated or undated empty pages with a cover, bought so its owner can write each day's events.
A printed picture of relatives held behind glass in a border of wood or metal, stood on a shelf or hung up.
A small flat disc of stamped metal issued by a government and used for payment in shops and machines.
A small adhesive paper label printed with a design and value, stuck to an envelope to pay for delivery.
A solid brick of refined gold stamped with its weight and purity, bought and stored as a lasting store of wealth.
A round gold or silver piece of fixed weight and purity, struck by a mint and valued mainly for its metal content.
A small metal badge with coloured glass-like inlay and a clasp on the back, pinned to a bag or jacket.
A bottle of fine red wine laid on its side in a cool dark room for years so it matures before opening.
A long flexible pole with a spool of line wound on a handle mechanism, used to cast a baited hook and pull fish from water.
A painted wooden or plastic model of a duck or similar bird floated or placed out to lure live birds within range.
A small hand-held reed or tube blown to imitate the cry of a deer, turkey or duck and draw animals closer.
A small platform or seat strapped high up a tree trunk from which a hunter waits quietly above the animals' line of sight.
A hard-wearing coat printed with blotchy green and brown shapes that help the wearer blend into woods and undergrowth.
A small spring-loaded base with a bait holder and snapping bar that catches and kills a mouse that disturbs it.
A flat mesh or plastic paddle on a long handle, swung to flatten flies and similar flying insects.
A set of door and window sensors wired to a loud siren that sounds when an intruder forces entry to a building.
A short metal chain fixed between a door and its frame so the door can be opened a crack without letting a visitor in.
A soft, lightweight blade-shaped item made of padded foam over a core, swung harmlessly in make-believe fights by children.
A small bendy bow with a string and suction-tipped or blunt arrows that children shoot gently at targets.
A long curved, single-edged blade with a wrapped handle, blunt or unsharpened, mounted on a rack on a wall for display.
A two-wheeled or four-wheeled covered box with a ramp and padded stalls, towed behind a car to carry horses.
A wheeled passenger cab on springs with a driver's seat and shafts, pulled along roads by one or more horses.
A narrow, runnered platform on which a rider stands or sits, pulled across snow by a team of harnessed dogs.
A small open boat with a mast, a sail and a centreboard, steered with a tiller by one or two people.
A tray on a single front wheel with two rear legs and two long handles, pushed by hand to move soil and bricks.
An upright metal frame on two wheels with a small lip at the bottom, tilted back to move heavy boxes by hand.
A shallow open tray on two or four wheels with a pull handle, hauled by hand to carry leaves, soil and plants.
A wire basket on a wheeled frame with a push handle, rolled around a store to carry goods being bought.
A zip-up case with an extending handle and small wheels on its base, pulled along behind a traveller carrying clothes.
A cutting machine with a seat, steering wheel and engine, driven across large lawns while blades under the body trim the grass.
A small engine-powered vehicle with a seat and rear hitch, driven to pull trailers, ploughs and rollers across a smallholding.
A wheeled truck with two steel prongs at the front that slide under crates on pallets, lifting and carrying them in warehouses.
A tracked machine with a cab, a long hydraulic arm and a bucket, driven to dig trenches and foundations in the ground.
A short wooden board on four small wheels, ridden standing up and pushed along with one foot on paths and ramps.
A low frame on two runners with a pull rope, on which a person slides downhill over snow.
A pair of boots with four small wheels each underneath, strapped on the feet to glide over smooth surfaces.
A narrow buoyant board of foam and fibreglass with fins, laid on and then stood upon to ride breaking waves.
A narrow, closed-deck boat with a cockpit, in which a seated paddler propels it using a two-bladed paddle.
A small battery-powered or foot-pushed plastic car with a seat and steering wheel that a young child sits in and drives.
A small pedal-less two-wheeled frame with a low seat that a toddler pushes along with their feet to learn to balance.
A long length of fabric worn over one shoulder and across the chest, forming a pouch in which an infant is carried.
A round or square container of clay or plastic with drainage holes, filled with compost to hold a growing plant.
A liquid or powder of nutrients mixed into water or soil to feed houseplants and flowers so they grow and bloom.
A lamp with bright full-spectrum bulbs, hung over seedlings indoors to give them the light they need to grow.
A thin cane or rod pushed into the soil beside a stem, to which the plant is tied for upright support.
A fitted shell of plastic, leather or silicone that snaps around a mobile handset to cushion it against drops and scratches.
A padded shoulder bag or backpack with adjustable inner dividers, made to carry a camera body, lenses and spare batteries safely.
A shaped hard or soft container with a lid, latches and a carrying handle that holds a guitar during transport.
A long padded or hard-shelled holder with a zip or latches and a lock, used to carry a rifle or shotgun.
A tall cylindrical bag with a stand and shoulder strap, divided inside to carry a full set of clubs and balls.
The empty rim and arms of plastic or metal that hold lenses in front of the eyes and rest on the nose and ears.
A hardened steel chain or U-shaped bar with a key or combination, used to fasten a bicycle to a rack.
A small disc of plastic or shell with holes, sewn onto a shirt and pushed through a slit to fasten it.
A strip of interlocking metal or plastic teeth with a sliding pull tab, sewn into trousers and bags to close an opening.
A thin insulated lead with a standard plug at each end, linking a computer to a phone or drive to carry data and power.
A mains plug adapter with a socket and lead that supplies regulated electric current to refill the battery of a handset.
A small cylindrical cell with a plus and minus end that stores chemical energy and supplies electric current to remote controls and clocks.
A length of insulated cable with a plug at one end and a block of several sockets at the other, reaching distant outlets.
A seat on a wheeled base with a padded back, adjustable height and swivel, made to be sat in for hours at a desk.
A broad flat table-top on legs or drawer units, with space for a computer and papers, at which people work.
A tall metal box with deep sliding drawers and a lock, in which hanging folders of papers are stored upright.
A self-supporting folding frame with two sides and a few flat rungs, climbed to reach shelves and ceilings.
A narrow, padded, height-adjustable folding surface on legs, on which shirts and sheets are laid to be pressed flat with a hot iron.
A small hand-cranked mill with a ceramic or steel burr inside a jar that crushes roasted beans to grounds.
A handle with a loop of curved wire strands at one end, moved briskly through eggs or cream to beat in air.
A heavy countertop motor with a tilting arm that drives a beater or dough hook around a locked bowl.
A hand-turned gadget with a cutting wheel and crank that clamps onto a tin's rim and cuts the lid away.
A tall glass jug with a lid and a plunger carrying a metal mesh disc, pressed down to separate brewed coffee from grounds.
An electric countertop machine that heats water and trickles it through ground coffee in a paper filter into a glass jug.
A hand-pushed box on wheels with rotating brushes inside that flick crumbs and dust from a rug into a small tray.
A long handle with a bundle of stiff bristles at one end, pushed over a floor to gather dust and litter.
A motorised machine with a hose or head that sucks dirt from floors and carpets into a bag or bin.
A folding frame of rails or a rack on which wet washing is hung indoors to dry without heat.
An electric drum that rotates damp washing in a stream of hot air until the cloth is dry.
A bundle of cotton strands or a sponge head on a long handle, dipped in water and dragged over a floor to clean it.
A small electric fan with plastic blades inside a cage on a stand, stood on a table and aimed at the user to cool them.
A set of thin slats joined by a pivot and spread open with a flick, waved in front of the face to stir air.
A glass or metal vessel holding lamp oil and a wick under a glass chimney, lit to give a steady flame of light.
A base topped with a shade and electric bulb and a switch, stood on a table to give local light.
A stone-like remnant of a plant or animal from ancient times, preserved in rock and dug up from the ground.
A naturally formed lump or cluster of crystals taken from the ground, kept for its colour, shape and rarity.
A cut, polished and unmounted piece of hard coloured mineral, such as a sapphire, kept loose rather than set in metal.
A piece of rock or metal that fell from space and landed on the Earth's surface.
The hard, often spiral outer casing left behind by a dead sea creature, found washed up on a beach.
A small smooth rounded stone worn down by water and picked up from a beach or riverbed.
A piece of wood bleached and smoothed by long soaking in sea or river water and washed up on a shore.
The branched bony growths shed each year from a stag's head, picked up in woods and kept as found.
A dead beetle or butterfly fixed by a pin through its body in a glass-topped case and labelled with its species.
The preserved skin of a dead bird or animal stretched over a form and posed with glass eyes to look alive.
The cleaned bony head of a dead animal such as a fox or cow, kept as found.
The tanned or dried skin of a cow, deer or sheep, with or without the hair left on.
A thin, hard square of fired clay or stone with a glazed or matt face, laid in rows over a floor with adhesive.
A small rectangular block of fired clay laid in courses with mortar to form walls.
Planks and beams of wood cut from felled trees and dried, kept in lengths for cutting and fixing into buildings.
A water-based liquid sold in tins that is brushed or rolled onto walls and ceilings to coat them in colour.
Short pointed pins of steel with a flat head, hammered into wood to hold pieces together.
Threaded metal pins with a slotted head, twisted into wood or plasterboard to hold things firmly together.
Threaded metal rods with a head at one end, pushed through holes and tightened with a nut to hold parts together.
A white or yellow sticky liquid squeezed from a bottle onto joints to bond pieces of timber when it dries.
A wide, strong, cloth-backed sticky tape, torn by hand, used for quick repairs and for sealing joints and bundles.
A flat rechargeable battery pack with a USB socket, carried to top up the charge of a phone while away from mains.
A thick lead with matching flat plugs at both ends, carrying picture and sound from a computer or player to a television.
Split and seasoned logs of wood cut to fit a stove or open fireplace and burned for heat.
Lumps of blackened, partly burnt wood sold in bags, lit in a grill to give an intense lasting heat for cooking.
A refillable steel bottle of compressed gas with a valve, connected by a hose to a heater or stove.
Thick fuel liquid delivered by tanker to a storage tank beside a house and pumped to a boiler to be burned for warmth.
A flat-sided steel or plastic container with a screw cap and handle for carrying petrol or water.
A strong-smelling liquid in a bottle with a child-proof cap, poured into water or onto surfaces to whiten cloth and kill germs.
Rolls of thin plastic sacks with drawstrings, filled with household rubbish, tied and put out for collection.
A roll of soft, thin, perforated paper kept near a lavatory and used to clean oneself after using it.
A hollow ball mounted on a tilted stand with a map of the world's land and seas printed on its surface.
A moulded plastic copy of a human torso or skeleton with removable organs, used to teach the parts of the body.
Flasks, beakers and test tubes of heat-resistant clear glass with measuring marks, used in laboratories to mix and heat liquids.
A small console with outdoor sensors that reads temperature, rain, wind and pressure and displays the figures indoors.
A pouch or box packed with a blanket, whistle, torch, first-aid supplies and food bars, kept ready for disasters.
A rectangular border of wood or metal with glass and a backing board, with nothing inserted, bought to hold a picture.
A painted or lit board hung above or beside a shop entrance that displays the name of the business.
A full-size jointed model of a human body, usually without a head, on which outfits are fitted and displayed in shops.
A papier-mâché container covered in coloured paper, filled with sweets and hung up to be burst open with a stick.
Tiny flakes of coloured paper or foil, thrown in handfuls over a couple or crowd at celebrations.
A compact motorised bed with a spinning chuck and a metal support bar, on which a piece of wood or metal is turned and cut.
A bench machine with a thin vertical blade moved rapidly up and down, guiding wood sheets past it to cut curves.
A pen-shaped electric heater with a hot metal tip that melts wire-like solder to join electronic parts.
A flat spinning disc driven by a motor or pedal, on which a lump of wet clay is shaped into a pot.
A hand-held pair of pincers with a rotating head of different-sized hollow tips, used to cut round holes in belts and straps.
A small hand frame holding a very thin blade, used to cut intricate shapes in sheet metal.
A boxed set of wooden pencils with graphite leads of graded hardness, used for sketching and shading drawings.
A basic yellow wooden pencil with a medium graphite core and a rubber at one end, used to write notes.
A large rectangle of thick absorbent looped cotton, used to dry the whole body after bathing or showering.
A small round mirror on a stand, often magnifying and lit around its edge, used to see the face closely when applying cosmetics.
A hand-held motorised unit with a rounded head that pulses rapidly against muscles to ease soreness after exertion.
A large rectangular slate-bedded table covered in green cloth with six pockets, on which cue balls are struck.
A taut round sheet of fabric stretched by springs on a steel frame outdoors, which people bounce up and down on.
A light frame covered with paper or cloth, flown on a long string so wind lifts it high in the air.
Cushioned lace-up shoes with a flexible, grippy sole and breathable upper, made to absorb impact over long distances on roads.
Sturdy ankle-high laced boots with thick treaded soles and waterproof uppers, worn to walk over rough, muddy or rocky ground.
A door lock fitted with a motor and radio link that opens by phone, code or fingerprint instead of a metal key.
A low disc-shaped machine that drives itself around a room on small wheels, sucking up dust and crumbs from the floor.
A long tube with lenses or mirrors that gathers light and magnifies distant objects such as planets and stars for viewing.
An instrument with lenses on a stand and a stage for slides that magnifies tiny specimens too small to see unaided.
A round lens in a rim with a handle, held over small print or objects to make them look larger.
A jar of live flour-and-water paste full of wild yeast and bacteria, fed regularly and mixed into dough to make it rise.
A rubbery pancake of bacteria and yeast floating in sweet tea, which ferments the liquid into a tangy fizzy drink.
A hand-held or backpack motor with a nozzle that forces a strong jet of air to push fallen leaves into piles.
A wheeled machine with a motor and rotating blade pushed across grass to cut it to an even height.
An engine coupled to an alternator in a frame, which burns fuel to produce mains-voltage electricity where no supply exists.
A flat platform with a display or dial, on which ingredients in a bowl are weighed to measure them for cooking.
A flat plate with a digital display that a person stands on to read their body weight.
A small vinyl figure of a film or comic character with an oversized head and black bead eyes, sold in a window box.
A light, slender, flexible steel blade with a blunted button tip and a small guard, used in a duelling contest scoring touches.
A set of seventy-eight illustrated cards, shuffled and dealt in layouts, used to seek insight or predict events.
A small battery-powered device implanted under the skin of the chest with wires to the heart, which sends pulses to keep its beat steady.
